findings.title: Canadian equity allocation significantly exceeds conservative target due to concentrated position
findings.detail: The Canadian equity allocation is {{m:alloc.CA_EQUITY.pct}}, significantly above the target of {{m:target.CA_EQUITY.pct}}. This is primarily driven by the Northshore Energy position in the non-registered account, which accounts for {{m:acct.NON_REG.value.cad}} of the total portfolio. This concentration conflicts with the conservative risk profile.

The US equity allocation is {{m:alloc.US_EQUITY.pct}}, which is below the target of {{m:target.US_EQUITY.pct}}. This drift of {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} exceeds the tolerance threshold, indicating a need to rebalance to align with the client's conservative investment strategy.
findings.title: US equity allocation is underweight relative to target portfolio

findings.detail: US equities experienced significant growth, with the index returning {{m:mkt.us_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date. This performance was primarily driven by a rally in technology sector stocks.
findings.title: US equity markets show strong year-to-date performance
Canadian equity performance impacted by energy sector volatility
findings.detail: Canadian equity performance was more moderate at {{m:mkt.ca_equity_ytd.pct}} percent. Volatility in the energy sector, which saw a {{m:mkt.energy_sector_qtd.pct}} percent decline quarter to date, contributed to this performance profile.

Canadian bond yields have drifted lower, with the ten-year yield currently at {{m:mkt.ca_10y_yield.pct}} percent. The bond index has returned {{m:mkt.ca_bond_ytd.pct}} percent year to date as inflation pressures have cooled.
findings.title: Canadian bond yields decline amid cooling inflation
International equity and real asset performance overview
findings.detail: International equities have returned {{m:mkt.intl_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date, while real assets, represented by the REIT index, have seen a return of {{m:mkt.reit_ytd.pct}} percent over the same period.

findings.title: No unused TFSA or RRSP contribution room available
findings.detail: The client has no unused contribution room in either TFSA or RRSP accounts, as indicated by {{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}} and {{m:tax.rrsp_room.cad}}. Consequently, no further tax-advantaged contributions can be made at this time.

The portfolio volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} exceeds the maximum allowable volatility of {{m:risk.vol_band_max.pct}} for a conservative profile. Given the client's age of sixty-eight and need for monthly income, this level of volatility is inappropriate and poses a significant risk to capital preservation.
findings.title: Portfolio volatility exceeds conservative suitability band
Excessive concentration in single security NRTH
findings.detail: The holding in NRTH represents {{m:conc.NRTH.pct}} of the portfolio, significantly exceeding the concentration limit of {{m:conc.limit.pct}}. This high exposure to a single security creates excessive idiosyncratic risk, which is unsuitable for a conservative investor requiring liquidity for monthly income.

In an equity bear market scenario, the portfolio would experience a loss of {{m:stress.equity_bear.cad}}, representing a {{m:stress.equity_bear.pct}} decline. This potential downside is substantial for a retiree with moderate liquidity needs, potentially impacting the ability to sustain monthly income draws.
findings.title: Significant downside risk in equity bear market scenario
